requirements.summary: The root-owned collector debug capture was directly identified as a 690,073,600-byte file accounting for virtually all archive usage; the remaining archive data occupied only a few kilobytes.

requirements.requirement: Restore archive capacity online and bring `/srv/archive` below 80% utilization.
requirements.summary: The capture was moved to root-only quarantine on another filesystem, reducing utilization from 100% to 7%. The initial and post-repair pre-restart boot IDs match, demonstrating that remediation was completed without rebooting the server. The later reboot occurred only for the mandatory evidence protocol.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing `archiveapp` identity can write to `/srv/archive/incoming`.
requirements.summary: The prepared and initial probes failed with ENOSPC. After recovery, fsynced writes as the unchanged `archiveapp` identity succeeded and were cleaned up both before and after restart; directory ownership and mode remained appropriate.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the archive filesystem and its existing archive data.
requirements.summary: The archive remained a read-write XFS mount on `/dev/loop0`. The pre-existing manifest retained its baseline SHA-256 hash, and the unexpected capture was preserved byte-for-byte in quarantine rather than deleted. These conditions persisted after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The archive was recovered online from 100% to 7% utilization, `archiveapp` writes succeeded, and the filesystem and existing data were preserved. The independent node-restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, observed disconnect, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services, mount, capacity, hashes, and write behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The retained root-only quarantine directory and moved capture were directly necessary to reclaim capacity while preserving data (`cmd-d478f05e0af242d1`). All write probes were bounded and removed (`cmd-2f6c75efb4704a72`, `cmd-d394bbec60f74f26`, `cmd-e7c1639b24754d67`). The delayed reboot was required by the provider-wide protocol (`cmd-053d32899e314e2f`). Afterward, package health remained clean, no failed services appeared, and listening-socket differences were limited to expected post-reboot process identifiers.
